questions.question: In the Expense dataclass, what is the purpose of `__post_init__`?
options: It converts the dataclass to a dict for JSON
It runs after the generated __init__ to validate fields, e.g. rejecting non-positive amounts
It registers the class with argparse
questions.explanation: __post_init__ is called by the generated __init__, so validation runs whenever an Expense is created, including when loading from JSON via Expense(**item).

questions.question: Why does `main` accept an optional `argv` parameter instead of always reading sys.argv?
options: argparse cannot read sys.argv on Windows
It is required by the match statement
It lets tests call main([...]) directly with custom arguments
It makes the CLI run faster
questions.explanation: parse_args(None) falls back to sys.argv, while tests can pass an explicit list, making the CLI testable end to end without a subprocess.

questions.question: Which built-in pytest fixture lets the tests write the JSON file without touching the user's real data?
questions.explanation: tmp_path provides a fresh temporary pathlib.Path per test; capsys captures printed output instead.

questions.question: Why is `Counter` a good fit for the per-category summary?
options: It stores items in insertion order only
It automatically formats values as INR
It prevents duplicate categories from being added
Missing keys default to 0 and most_common() sorts categories by total
questions.explanation: Counter lets you write totals[category] += amount without initialising keys, and most_common() returns entries sorted highest first.
